faqs.question: Who can become a captain?
faqs.answer: Any player who creates a team through the registration form becomes its captain. If you joined a team without being the captain, you can then request the role from your player hub — the current captain or the staff approves the handover.

faqs.question: How many captains per team?
faqs.answer: Only one official captain at a time. They receive match check-ins, staff notifications and messages from other teams. The handover can be done at any time from the dashboard.

faqs.question: What happens if I don’t respond in time to a scrim or a check-in?
faqs.answer: Match check-ins have a strict window (~1h before kickoff) — without validation, the team is declared a forfeit. Scrims carry no penalty, but a quick refusal helps the community get organized.

faqs.question: Can I manage several teams?
faqs.answer: No, a player can only be captain of one team at a time. It’s a safeguard to avoid schedule conflicts and guarantee the captain’s availability during tournament phases.

faqs.question: What happens if I leave my team?
faqs.answer: If you’re not the captain, you can leave freely (the captain and the staff are notified). If you’re the captain, hand the armband to another member first, otherwise the staff will ask you to do so before approving your departure.

inscription2026.heroTitle: How to register your team for the 2026 women's tournament
inscription2026.heroSubtitle: Follow these steps to join the 2026 edition of the OW Women's Cup. Roster, captain, BattleTag: here's everything you need.
inscription2026.prereq1Desc: Sign up with your email or via Discord. You'll use this account to manage your team and your matches.
inscription2026.prereq2Desc: Format Name#0000. Required for every player on the roster — it's used for custom-game invites.
inscription2026.prereq3Desc: 5v5 Role Queue line-up: 1 Tank, 2 DPS, 2 Support. You can add up to 2 substitutes.
inscription2026.prereq4Desc: A lead player who validates match sheets, handles check-in and receives staff communications.
inscription2026.stepsIntro: Count about ten minutes if all players are ready. You can pause and resume at any time from your account.
inscription2026.step1Desc: Sign up for free with your email or Discord account. Remember to add your BattleTag right when you create it.
inscription2026.step2Desc: Gather 5 starting players (1 Tank, 2 DPS, 2 Support). You can prepare their emails and BattleTags in advance to go faster at registration time.
inscription2026.step3Desc: The captain is the official point of contact between the team and the staff. They receive match notifications and report results.
inscription2026.step4Desc: Enter your team's name, tag, country and logo, then add all players at once. Your team is automatically registered for the 2026 women's tournament.
inscription2026.step5Desc: All announcements, schedules and confirmations go through the official Discord. The captain's presence there is mandatory.
inscription2026.finalBody: The form handles everything: account, roster and registration for the 2026 women's tournament.
inscription2026.faq1A: Yes, the 2026 edition is 100% women. All participants must identify as women (cis or trans) and non-binary people are welcome, in line with the association's charter.
inscription2026.faq2A: No minimum rank: the tournament welcomes all levels. The Swiss format lets you face teams of a similar level round after round.
inscription2026.faq3Q: Can I register alone, without a team?
inscription2026.faq3A: Registration is by team. If you're looking for a roster, hop on the Discord: a dedicated recruitment channel helps you find teammates.
inscription2026.faq4Q: Can I change my roster after registering?
inscription2026.faq4A: Yes, as long as check-ins aren't locked. Changes are made from your team page. After the deadline, contact the staff on Discord.
inscription2026.faq5A: No, registration for the 2026 women's tournament is free. The association runs on donations and partnerships.
inscription2026.helpBody: A question about your roster, a BattleTag causing trouble, or need an exception? The staff replies on Discord and by email.

jeuxPage.overwatchTagline: The title that founded the community.
jeuxPage.overwatchPitch: Blizzard's hero shooter has been the heart of the OW Women's Cup since 2025. Full map veto, a 29-map pool and BO1/3/5 formats for the playoffs.
jeuxPage.valorantPitch: Riot's tactical shooter plugs into our tournament stack with its competitive pool (Ascent, Bind, Lotus, Sunset…) and a veto based on the VCT ruleset.
jeuxPage.cs2Pitch: Counter-Strike 2 uses the ESL / Major veto sequences (ban-ban-pick-pick-ban-ban-decider) on the official active-duty maps.
jeuxPage.r6Pitch: Rainbow Six Siege joins the lineup with its full ranked pool (Bank, Clubhouse, Kafe, Nighthaven Labs…) and a veto tuned to esports rules.
jeuxPage.marvelPitch: Marvel Rivals features Domination, Convoy and Convergence across an 11-map pool: BO1/3/5 tournaments with a veto to rule out home-turf maps.
jeuxPage.rocketPitch: Rocket League skips the veto (fixed arena) but runs long BO3/5/7 formats for the playoffs: the tournament stack handles the match directly, no veto needed.
jeuxPage.lolPitch: League of Legends uses the official Tournament Draft: 10 bans + 10 picks split across two phases. The bot runs the draft on Discord and pushes it to the live UI.
jeuxPage.dota2Pitch: Dota 2 uses Captains Mode (patch 7.34+): 9 bans + 10 picks across three phases, handled end to end by our multi-game draft engine.
jeuxPage.fallbackPitch: Game supported by the multi-game tournament stack: automated registration, bracket, scoring and Discord match threads.

jeuxPage.step1Detail: Create your team, pick your game and your format. The platform checks the roster and slots you into the bracket as soon as registration opens.
jeuxPage.step2Detail: Before every match, the tool runs the veto or draft (depending on the game) with a timer, automatic turn order and full history. No staff needed.
jeuxPage.step3Detail: The bot opens a dedicated thread, posts the scoreboard, records the scores and closes the match. Casters and viewers follow along live.
jeuxPage.botDesc: Everything runs through slash commands: registration, match, veto, draft, score, dispute. One interface, identical across every game.
jeuxPage.cap1Detail: Creation, publishing, registrations, roster management. The /tournoi creer command lets you pick from all 8 games.
jeuxPage.cap2Detail: The bot opens a Discord thread per match, tracks check-in, collects the scores and automatically pushes the win through the bracket.
jeuxPage.cap3Detail: Automated veto in DMs with the captains: turn order, timer, game-specific ESL/VCT sequences. No manual input from staff.
jeuxPage.cap4Detail: Tournament Draft (LoL) and Captains Mode (Dota 2) handled end to end: bans, picks, fearless draft, server timer and a live spectator UI.
jeuxPage.cap5Detail: Caster coordination, match-to-cast assignments, multi-channel announcements and Twitch stream relays.
jeuxPage.cap6Detail: Public scrim creation, opponent finding, dedicated thread and automatic reminders. Works for every game in the registry.
jeuxPage.cap7Detail: Dedicated dispute forum, tracked by the refereeing staff with notifications to captains at every update.
jeuxPage.cap8Detail: Live tournament standings, stats aggregated per team and player, match history with veto/draft replays.
jeuxPage.cap9Detail: Context-aware help per command, an /aide-tournoi channel for staff and bot registration on other servers.
jeuxPage.multiTenantBody: the bot can run on several Discord servers with full isolation of tournaments, teams and stats. Handy if another org wants the same stack.
jeuxPage.inviteBotCta: Invite the bot to my server
jeuxPage.faqIntroAfter: channel on Discord is open to every captain.
jeuxPage.faq1Question: My favourite game isn't on the list — can you add it?
jeuxPage.faq1Answer: Yes — the stack is built for it. Adding a game means declaring its registry (map pool or draft flow, supported formats) and updating the /tournoi creer command. Expect one to two weeks depending on complexity. Start a conversation via the Contact page and we'll talk it through.
jeuxPage.faq2Question: How exactly does the map veto work?
jeuxPage.faq2Answer: The bot DMs both captains as soon as the match is ready. Each captain bans or picks in turn following the game's sequence (ESL/Major for CS2, VCT for Valorant, etc.), on a server-side timer. The sequence is replayed in the Discord thread and stored in the match history.
jeuxPage.faq3Question: Why do only LoL and Dota 2 have a hero draft?
jeuxPage.faq3Answer: Because those two games have a real, formalised draft phase (Tournament Draft for LoL, Captains Mode for Dota 2) where bans and picks alternate. Hero shooters like Overwatch or Marvel Rivals allow free hero swapping mid-game: there's nothing to draft before the match.
jeuxPage.faq4Question: Can the bot run on other Discord servers?
jeuxPage.faq4Answer: Yes. The bot is multi-tenant: you can invite it to any server. Each server has its own tournaments, teams and stats, isolated by a tenant identifier. The “Invite the bot to my server” button above kicks off the self-service flow.
jeuxPage.faq5Question: Which format should I pick for my tournament?
jeuxPage.faq5Answer: BO1 = single game (fast, ideal for group stages). BO3 = competitive standard, first to two maps out of three. BO5 = grand finals. BO7 = Rocket League only (motorsport, short games). You can mix formats: for example BO1 in groups and BO3 in the bracket.
jeuxPage.faq6Question: How much does it cost to use the system?
jeuxPage.faq6Answer: Nothing. The stack is open and the OW Women's Cup association maintains it as a community tool. You can join our tournaments, or invite the bot to your own server if you run your own — either way there's no licence fee.
jeuxPage.faq7Question: Can I follow matches live without installing the bot?
jeuxPage.faq7Answer: Yes: every public match is viewable on this site (bracket, scores, veto and draft replays) and Twitch casts are relayed on the Live page. The bot is a tool for players and staff, not a requirement for the audience.
jeuxPage.ctaTitle: Want us to add your game?
jeuxPage.ctaDesc: The stack is built to welcome new titles. If your game's women's scene deserves a tournament as well-equipped as ours, tell us — we'll look into it together.

developpeursPage.heroSubtitle: A public, read-only REST API to consume tournament, match, team, standings and league data. No key, versioned, ready to drop into your overlays, bots and sites.

developpeursPage.card1Body: Read routes are plain GETs, no key. Writing, by contrast, requires a scoped token (see below).

developpeursPage.card4Body: Prefixed with /api/public/v1. v1 stays stable; any breaking change ships as v2.
developpeursPage.card5Body: Around 120 requests per minute per IP address. Beyond that: a RATE_LIMITED error.
developpeursPage.card6Body: The payload always sits under { data: ... }. Lists add a pagination object.

developpeursPage.card7Body: A scoped Bearer pk_live_… token unlocks writes: match result reporting, with more to come.
developpeursPage.card8Body: A single GraphQL endpoint: anonymous queries, mutations on a scoped token.
developpeursPage.writeSectionIntro: Alongside anonymous reads, a write surface lets third-party organisers automate their operations (result reporting, overlays, integrations). Every request is authenticated with a scoped token.
developpeursPage.writeAccessBody: API keys are self-service: an admin of your organisation creates them from the admin area (Settings → API keys). Each key carries its scopes and is shown only once at creation. Public reads stay open to everyone, no key required.
developpeursPage.writeAuthBody: Every write carries an Authorization: Bearer pk_live_… header. Tokens are issued by an organisation admin from the admin area and shown only once at creation. The target tenant is derived from the token — no extra header is needed.
developpeursPage.writeScopesIntro: A token carries a list of scopes in resource:action form. Each endpoint declares the scope it requires; a missing scope returns 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE. There is no implication: matches:write does not grant matches:read.
developpeursPage.writeErrorsIntro: Writes share the { error, code } envelope and add the following codes to the read codes above.
developpeursPage.errInsufficientScope: Valid token, but the required scope is missing.
developpeursPage.errMaintenanceMode: Writes frozen: the site is in maintenance mode.
developpeursPage.errConflict: State conflict (e.g. a match already closed).
developpeursPage.writeErrorsNote: The read codes (NOT_FOUND, BAD_REQUEST, RATE_LIMITED, INTERNAL…) apply as well.
developpeursPage.writeIdempotencyBody: Send an Idempotency-Key header (≤ 200 characters) to make retries safe. A 2xx response is cached for 5 minutes and replayed verbatim (Idempotency-Replay: true header) for the same key and the same body.
developpeursPage.writeEndpointSummary: Sets the final score of a match (direct authority, no captain consensus). The match moves to the finished status, the bracket is propagated and notifications are sent. Idempotent.
developpeursPage.graphqlSectionIntro: A single POST /api/graphql endpoint serves the GraphQL API. Queries are anonymous, like the read REST API; mutations require a scoped token.
developpeursPage.graphqlDepthNote: GraphiQL and introspection are available in development only. Query depth is capped at 8 levels.

appPage.installStep1Body: Chrome or Edge → install icon on the right of the address bar, OR menu ⋮ → "Install app".
appPage.installStep2Body: Chrome → menu ⋮ → "Add to home screen". The app appears like a normal app.
appPage.installStep3Body: Safari → Share button ↗ → "Add to home screen". iOS ≥ 16.4 for notifications.
appPage.installStep4Body: Chrome or Edge support standalone install (menu ⋮ → "Install"). Firefox: not yet.
appPage.faq1Q: Which devices does it work on?
appPage.faq1A: Windows 11 (Edge / Chrome), macOS, Linux, Android and iOS ≥ 16.4. On iOS, some features (taskbar badge, action buttons) are limited by Apple — the essentials work everywhere.
appPage.faq2A: From this page or any page of the site: click the install icon on the right of the address bar, or open the Chrome / Edge menu → "Install app". On Android, "Add to home screen". On iOS, share → "Add to home screen".
appPage.faq3Q: Why not a real app on the Store?
appPage.faq3A: A PWA avoids Apple / Google Play fees, validation delays, and delivers updates in seconds (vs days on the stores). The code runs in the browser — no 80 MB download, no intrusive system permissions.
appPage.faq4A: None. The PWA is exactly the same site, just pinned as an icon. We store your session token (Supabase auth) locally so you don't have to log in every time, and that's all.
appPage.faq5A: On Windows: right-click the taskbar icon → Uninstall. On macOS: from the app menu → Uninstall. Android: long-press the icon → Uninstall. Your data stays on the site (the PWA is just a shortcut).
appPage.faq6Q: Can I enable notifications without installing?
appPage.faq6A: Yes — from your admin / caster / player space, the notification enablement banner also works in a regular browser. Installing just adds the taskbar icon, shortcuts and offline mode.

rulesPage.heroSubtitle: A summary of the competitive Overwatch settings used for the OW Women's Cup. The whole event is built on Blizzard's official rules, adapted to the tournament format.
rulesPage.section1Item2: Unique heroes: no duplicates allowed within the same team.
rulesPage.section1Item3: Current patch: every game is played on the latest live version of Overwatch (no rollbacks).
rulesPage.section1Item4: Workshop items, mods, macros and scripts are forbidden.
rulesPage.section2Item2: Score capped per mode (e.g. Control in BO3).
rulesPage.section2Item4: Technical pause: only for a bug or disconnection, max 5 min per team.
rulesPage.section3Item1: No exploits, stream sniping or account sharing.
rulesPage.section3Item2: Voice and text chat are subject to the Blizzard Code of Conduct.
rulesPage.section3Item3: Dispute resolution: final decision by the tournament referees.
rulesPage.section3Item4: Joining the tournament Discord is mandatory: https://discord.gg/gERSsjC3Vd
rulesPage.modesNote: Applies with the « Competitive rules » preset in custom games.
rulesPage.mode1Rules: BO3 across three control points. If 1-1, a decider is played. Overtime if a team contests or is about to capture.
rulesPage.mode2Rules: Att/Def: capture point A then escort the payload. Best progression wins; overtime if progression is contested.
rulesPage.mode3Rules: Att/Def: pure payload escort to the final point. If tied after both rounds, play resumes with a time bank; the greater distance breaks the tie.
rulesPage.mode4Rules: Successive capture points, first to 2 points. Overtime if a point is contested. Ultimates reset on each capture.
rulesPage.mode5Rules: Winning team: the furthest distance pushed. Overtime if the robot is contested or close to the opponent's marker.
rulesPage.referencesNote: Check the official documents for updates to rules, maps or patches.
